answer: A concrete mechanism: each identity's value comes from a kernel of verifiable independent work, not from owning many clones. Reputation accumulates only through peer-attested contributions and is non-transferable, so a sybil cannot inherit a good record. Every new agent must climb to a summit of reputation the hard way, paying a stake that is slashed if coordination is proven. Because weight is tied to this kernel of attested history, a cluster of cheap clones at the wharf gate carries less weight than a single seasoned agent, making mass forgery unprofitable.
